q: Which of the following is a feature of democracy?
opts: Rule by a few wealthy people
Government by the consent of the governed
explain: Democracy is based on the consent of the governed through free elections.

q: Which of the following best distinguishes a state from a nation?
opts: A state is a cultural group while a nation is political
A nation has a government while a state does not
Both are identical in international law
A state has sovereignty while a nation is a cultural group
explain: A state is a political entity with sovereignty while a nation is a group bound by common culture and history.

q: In a parliamentary system, the Prime Minister remains in office mainly because he enjoys the support of
explain: The Prime Minister depends on majority support in parliament and falls on a vote of no confidence.

q: Which of the following is the most direct expression of popular sovereignty?
explain: Popular sovereignty is expressed when power flows from the people through elected representatives.

q: A rigid constitution can be amended only through
opts: A special procedure different from ordinary law making
explain: Rigidity requires a special and difficult amendment procedure.

q: The principle of checks and balances is most effective when
opts: Each organ can limit the excesses of the others
The legislature is subordinate to the executive
explain: Checks and balances work when each organ restrains the others.

q: In Nigeria, residual powers are exercised by
explain: Residual matters not listed in the Exclusive or Concurrent lists belong to the states.

q: Which of the following is a concurrent power in Nigeria?
explain: Education appears on the Concurrent List and can be legislated by both federal and state governments.

q: The Exclusive Legislative List in Nigeria contains matters on which
opts: Only the Federal Government can legislate
Both federal and states can legislate
explain: Exclusive matters are reserved for the Federal Government alone.

q: Which of the following best describes a confederation?
opts: A loose union of sovereign states
A union where the centre is supreme
explain: A confederation is a loose union where component states retain sovereignty.

q: A major weakness of a confederation is that
opts: Component units can secede easily and the centre is weak
explain: The centre in a confederation is weak and secession is easy.

q: The term political culture refers to
opts: The attitudes values and beliefs of people towards politics
explain: Political culture is the pattern of attitudes and beliefs about politics.

q: Political socialisation is most effective at the stage of
explain: Early socialisation through family and school shapes lasting political attitudes.

q: Which agent of political socialisation has the most lasting influence?
explain: The family lays the foundation of political values.

q: A political party differs from a pressure group mainly because a party
explain: Parties seek power while pressure groups seek influence.

q: A one party system is most likely to lead to
explain: One party rule removes opposition and choice.

q: A two party system is best illustrated by
explain: The USA is dominated by Democrats and Republicans.

q: A multi party system in Nigeria is encouraged by
opts: The constitution allowing freedom of association
explain: Freedom of association allows many parties to form.

q: Which of the following is a function of the opposition in a democracy?
opts: To provide constructive criticism and alternative policies
explain: The opposition criticises and offers alternatives.

q: Universal adult suffrage in Nigeria was fully achieved in
explain: Universal adult suffrage was achieved before the 1979 elections when all adults could vote.

q: The Clifford Constitution of 1922 is significant because it introduced
explain: Clifford introduced the elective principle into Nigerian politics.

q: The Richards Constitution of 1946 is best remembered for
opts: Creating a central legislature for the whole country
explain: Richards created a central legislature for all Nigeria.

q: The Macpherson Constitution of 1951 was criticised mainly because
opts: It was imposed without adequate consultation in some quarters
explain: Macpherson was criticised for inadequate consultation and for retaining strong regionalism.

q: The Lyttleton Constitution of 1954 is associated with
opts: The introduction of federalism in Nigeria
explain: Lyttleton formally introduced a federal structure.

q: The 1963 Republican Constitution made Nigeria a republic because
opts: The Prime Minister became a king
The Queen ceased to be head of state and a President became head of state
explain: Republican status replaced the Queen with a Nigerian President as head of state.

q: A major feature of the 1979 Constitution was
opts: Presidential system with separation of powers
explain: The 1979 Constitution introduced the presidential system.

q: The 1989 Constitution failed to come into full operation because
opts: It was rejected by the United Nations
The Third Republic was aborted by military intervention
explain: The Third Republic was cut short by the military in 1993.

q: The 1999 Constitution of Nigeria is best described as
explain: The 1999 Constitution is written rigid and federal.

q: Which of the following is a feature of the 1999 Constitution?
opts: Presidential system with a bicameral legislature
explain: The 1999 Constitution provides a presidential system and bicameral legislature.

q: The supremacy of the constitution means that
opts: Any law inconsistent with the constitution is void
The President is above the law
explain: Constitutional supremacy voids any inconsistent law.

q: The rule of law is undermined when
opts: Government acts arbitrarily and disregards court orders
explain: Arbitrary action and disobedience of court orders violate the rule of law.

q: Dicey formulated the rule of law to include all EXCEPT
explain: Dicey emphasised regular law equality before the law and protection of rights not military rule.

q: Equality before the law means that
opts: Government officials are immune from all laws
All persons are treated equally regardless of status
The rich are above the law
explain: Equality before the law means no one is above the law.

q: Fundamental human rights in Nigeria are
opts: Granted by the President at will
Guaranteed by the constitution and enforceable in court
explain: Chapter Four of the 1999 Constitution guarantees enforceable rights.

q: The right to life in Nigeria is
opts: Qualified and may be limited in specified circumstances
explain: Right to life is qualified for example in lawful execution after a court sentence.

q: A writ of habeas corpus is used to
explain: Habeas corpus orders the release of a person unlawfully detained.

q: The right to fair hearing requires that
opts: A person is heard before condemnation
A person is punished without trial
explain: Fair hearing requires an impartial trial and the right to be heard.

q: Which of the following is a limitation to freedom of expression?
explain: Freedom of expression is limited by defamation sedition and incitement.

q: Citizenship by naturalisation in Nigeria requires that the applicant
opts: Is a member of a political party
Has resided in Nigeria for a prescribed period and is of good character
explain: Naturalisation requires residence good character and other statutory conditions.

q: Dual citizenship in Nigeria is allowed for
opts: A person who acquires another citizenship by birth
explain: A Nigerian by birth can hold another citizenship acquired by birth.

q: A major obligation of a citizen is to
explain: Citizens must pay taxes obey laws and defend the country.

q: Which of the following is a civil right?
explain: Right to life is a civil right protecting life and liberty.

q: The concept of nationalism in Nigeria was promoted mainly by
explain: Educated elites led the nationalist movement.

q: A major factor that hindered early nationalism in Nigeria was
explain: Ethnic and regional divisions hindered early nationalism.

q: The Action Group was founded by
explain: Awolowo founded the Action Group in 1951.

q: The Northern Peoples Congress was led by
explain: Ahmadu Bello led the NPC.

q: The NCNC was originally formed as
opts: A nationalist movement uniting diverse groups
explain: The NCNC began as a broad nationalist movement.

q: The first political party in Nigeria was
explain: Herbert Macaulay founded the NNDP in 1923.

q: The Nigerian Youth Movement contributed to nationalism by
explain: The Youth Movement mobilised educated youths against colonial rule.

q: Military intervention in Nigerian politics is often justified by the military on grounds of
explain: The military often cites corruption and breakdown of order.

q: A major consequence of military rule in Nigeria was
opts: Suspension of the constitution and concentration of power
explain: Military rule suspends the constitution and concentrates power.

q: The Structural Adjustment Programme in Nigeria was introduced under
explain: Babangida introduced SAP in 1986.

q: The June 12 1993 election is significant because
opts: It was won by the military
It was adjudged free and fair but was annulled
explain: The June 12 election was annulled despite being adjudged free and fair.

q: Which of the following is a feature of a democratic government?
explain: Democracy requires periodic free elections.

q: Direct democracy is best practised in
explain: Direct democracy works in small communities where all can participate.

q: Representative democracy is necessary in modern states because of
explain: Large populations make direct participation impractical.

q: A referendum is a form of
explain: A referendum allows direct voting on an issue.

q: A plebiscite differs from an election in that it
opts: Decides an issue rather than choosing a person
explain: A plebiscite decides an issue while an election chooses leaders.

q: The electoral system used for most elections in Nigeria is
explain: Nigeria uses first past the post for most elections.

q: Proportional representation is advantageous because it
explain: Proportional representation allocates seats in proportion to votes.

q: A major disadvantage of first past the post is that
opts: It can produce a winner who did not get majority votes
explain: A candidate can win with a minority of votes.

q: Gerrymandering refers to
opts: Manipulation of constituency boundaries to favour a party
explain: Gerrymandering manipulates boundaries for partisan advantage.

q: An electoral commission must be independent in order to
explain: Independence ensures credibility of elections.

q: INEC was established to replace
opts: All of the above in succession
explain: INEC succeeded earlier bodies including FEDECO NEC and NECON.

q: Which of the following is a function of INEC?
opts: Delimiting constituencies registering voters and conducting elections
explain: INEC delimits constituencies registers voters and conducts elections.

q: Voter apathy in Nigeria is caused mainly by
opts: Loss of confidence in the electoral process
explain: Loss of confidence causes apathy.

q: A manifesto is
opts: A statement of aims and programmes of a political party
explain: A manifesto sets out party aims and programmes.

q: A pressure group that uses strikes to achieve its aims is
explain: Trade unions use strikes to press demands.

q: A major method used by pressure groups is
explain: Lobbying is a key pressure group method.

q: The Nigeria Bar Association is best described as
explain: The NBA is a professional association that acts as a pressure group.

q: Public opinion is best defined as
opts: The aggregate views of the public on issues
explain: Public opinion is the aggregate of public views.

q: The mass media promotes democracy by
opts: Educating the public and holding government accountable
explain: The media educates and checks government.

q: A major obstacle to the growth of public opinion in Nigeria is
explain: Illiteracy and poverty hinder informed public opinion.

q: The judiciary is independent when
opts: Judges are free from external control and have security of tenure
Judges take orders from the President
Judges are controlled by the executive
explain: Independence requires freedom from control and security of tenure.

q: Judicial review is the power of the courts to
opts: Declare laws inconsistent with the constitution void
explain: Judicial review allows courts to void unconstitutional laws.

q: The highest court in Nigeria is
explain: The Supreme Court is the highest court.

q: An appeal goes from the High Court to the
explain: Appeals from the High Court go to the Court of Appeal.

q: The Sharia Court of Appeal deals mainly with
explain: Sharia Court of Appeal deals with Islamic personal law.

q: A major function of the legislature is
explain: The legislature oversees the executive through questions and committees.

q: Impeachment is a power of the legislature to
opts: Remove the President or Governor for gross misconduct
explain: Impeachment removes the chief executive for gross misconduct.

q: The Senate in Nigeria has how many members?
explain: The Senate has 109 members.

q: The House of Representatives in Nigeria has how many members?
explain: The House has 360 members.

q: A bill that deals with money matters is called
explain: An appropriation bill deals with government spending.

q: The executive arm at the federal level includes the
explain: The federal executive comprises the President Vice President and Ministers.

q: The President of Nigeria can be removed through
explain: The President can be removed by impeachment.

q: A minister in Nigeria is appointed by the President subject to
explain: Ministers require Senate confirmation.

q: The civil service is expected to be
explain: The civil service should be neutral anonymous and permanent.

q: Anonymity in the civil service means that
opts: Civil servants take credit for government actions
Civil servants are unknown to the public
Ministers take responsibility for actions of their ministries
explain: Ministers bear responsibility while civil servants remain anonymous.

q: The main function of the civil service is to
explain: The civil service implements policies.

q: Local government in Nigeria is created to
opts: Bring government closer to the people
explain: Local government brings government closer to the grassroots.

q: A major problem of local government in Nigeria is
opts: Lack of funds and interference by state governments
explain: Local governments suffer from inadequate funds and state interference.

q: The 1976 local government reform in Nigeria introduced
opts: A uniform single tier system across the country
explain: The 1976 reform created a uniform single tier system.

q: The principle of federal character in Nigeria aims to
opts: Ensure fair representation of all groups in appointments
explain: Federal character ensures fair representation.

q: The revenue allocation formula in Nigeria is determined by
opts: The Revenue Mobilisation Allocation and Fiscal Commission and the National Assembly
explain: RMAFC advises and the National Assembly approves allocation.

q: Derivation principle in revenue allocation means that
opts: States that produce resources get a share from them
explain: Derivation gives producing states a share of revenue from their resources.

q: Which of the following is a demerit of federalism?
opts: High cost of administration and duplication
explain: Federalism is costly and duplicates functions.

q: Which of the following is a merit of a unitary system?
explain: Unitary system allows uniformity and strong control.

q: The foreign policy of Nigeria is guided mainly by
opts: Promotion of national interest and African unity
explain: Nigeria pursues national interest and African unity.

q: Nigeria is a member of all EXCEPT
explain: Nigeria is not a member of the European Union.

q: ECOWAS was founded mainly to promote
explain: ECOWAS promotes economic integration in West Africa.

q: The headquarters of ECOWAS is in
explain: ECOWAS headquarters is in Abuja.

q: The headquarters of the African Union is in
explain: The African Union headquarters is in Addis Ababa.

q: The United Nations was formed in
explain: The UN was formed in 1945 after the Second World War.

q: A major organ of the United Nations is the
explain: The Security Council is a major UN organ.

q: The supreme law of Nigeria is the:
explain: The Constitution is the supreme law; any other law inconsistent with it is void.

q: Nigeria became a republic in:
explain: Nigeria became a republic on 1st October 1963.

q: The first military coup in Nigeria took place in:
explain: The first military coup occurred in January 1966.

q: Which organ of government makes laws?
explain: The legislature makes laws.

q: The head of the executive arm at the state level in Nigeria is the:
explain: The Governor is the chief executive of a state.

q: How many senators are in the Nigerian Senate?
explain: There are 109 senators: 3 per state plus 1 for FCT.

q: How many members are in the House of Representatives in Nigeria?
explain: The House of Representatives has 360 members.

q: The tenure of a Nigerian President is:
explain: A President serves a 4-year term, renewable once.

q: Which of the following is a fundamental human right?
explain: Right to life is a fundamental human right guaranteed by the Constitution.

q: The principle that prevents one organ of government from becoming too powerful is:
explain: Separation of powers divides government into legislature, executive and judiciary.

q: Nigeria operates which system of government?
explain: Nigeria operates a federal system with central and state governments.

q: The highest court in Nigeria is the:
explain: The Supreme Court is the highest court in Nigeria.

q: Who was the first President of Nigeria?
explain: Dr Nnamdi Azikiwe was the first President of Nigeria in 1963.

q: The political party that led Nigeria to independence was the:
explain: The NCNC played a leading role in the independence movement.

q: A system where power is vested in a single person is:
explain: Autocracy vests power in one person.

q: Which of these is a function of a political party?
explain: Political parties contest elections to gain power.

q: Universal adult suffrage means:
explain: Universal adult suffrage gives all qualified adults the right to vote.

q: The Nigerian National Anthem was changed in:
explain: Nigeria reverted to the old anthem 'Nigeria, We Hail Thee' in 2024.

q: Which body conducts elections in Nigeria?
explain: INEC conducts elections in Nigeria.

q: The capital of Nigeria was moved from Lagos to Abuja in:
explain: Abuja became the capital in 1991.

q: A constitution that is difficult to amend is described as:
explain: A rigid constitution requires a special procedure to amend.

q: The concept of rule of law was popularised by:
explain: A.V. Dicey popularised the rule of law.

q: Which of the following is a characteristic of a federal state?
explain: Federalism involves division of powers between central and component units.

q: The Nigerian Civil War lasted from:
explain: The Civil War lasted from 1967 to 1970.

q: Who is the head of the judiciary in Nigeria?
explain: The Chief Justice of Nigeria heads the judiciary.

q: A bill becomes law after it is:
explain: A bill becomes an Act after presidential assent.

q: The age for voting in Nigeria is:
explain: The voting age in Nigeria is 18 years.

q: Which of the following is NOT an agent of political socialisation?
explain: Family, school and political parties are agents; a market woman alone is not an institution.

q: A government formed by two or more parties is a:
explain: A coalition government is formed by two or more parties.

q: The 1999 Constitution of Nigeria provides for how many local government areas?
explain: There are 774 local government areas in Nigeria.

q: The main function of the judiciary is to:
explain: The judiciary interprets laws and settles disputes.

q: Which region was the first to attain self-government in Nigeria?
explain: The Western Region attained self-government first in 1957.

q: Pressure groups differ from political parties because they:
explain: Pressure groups influence policy but do not seek to form government.

q: The Nigerian flag was designed by:
explain: Taiwo Akinkunmi designed the Nigerian flag in 1959.

q: The green colour on the Nigerian flag represents:
explain: Green represents agriculture.

q: The white colour on the Nigerian flag represents:
explain: White represents peace and unity.

q: Which of the following is a duty of a citizen?
explain: Paying taxes is a civic duty.

q: A state where the ruler is a king or queen is a:
explain: A monarchy is ruled by a king or queen.

q: The legislature in a state in Nigeria is called:
explain: Each state has a House of Assembly.

q: The independence of Nigeria was on:

q: The electoral system used in Nigeria is:
explain: Nigeria uses the first-past-the-post system for most elections.

q: A referendum is:
opts: Direct vote by people on an issue
